Pin the chain with a @SpringBootTest that sets ONLY the shared property and asserts the new client reaches the stub - a placeholder typo is otherwise invisible until the rig. (3) For a FAIL-CLOSED-TO-EMPTY edge (the base-scope SPI shape, mx-1ce7d5) the guard body must RETURN the empty list for permanent failures rather than throw a permanent carrier the caller maps: Resilience4jCallGuard records onError for ANY thrown exception, retryable or not, so throwing would count a decision as a transport failure (mx-951d2f). Only the transient carrier (5xx/429/timeout/refused) is thrown. Asserted directly: N alternating 404/empty-array responses leave the breaker CLOSED with getNumberOfFailedCalls()==0, while a thrown transient outage does open it - and an open breaker still returns empty, never a throw. Relates to mx-24ac37 (the B3-preserving wrapper shape this varies) and mx-951d2f.

SUPERVISED-SCOPE T5 ★-gate finding. A list that composes TWO id sets (team membership M, plus a derived second scope) picks ONE anchor id to resolve the residual-driving role on, because the library's findAuthorized compiles exactly one residual from the one AbacContext it is given. The design's rule 'whenever M is non-empty, anchor on a MEMBERSHIP id' is necessary but NOT sufficient: it constrains the id, not the ROLE resolved on it, and the two are read at different instants. If the membership on the anchor is revoked between reading the governed ids and resolving the role, the user-service's ordered fallthrough (membership first, supervision second) answers with the SYNTHESIZED supervisor role - whose VACUOUS tag requirement then drives the residual over EVERY OTHER membership row still in scope. That is exactly the fail-open the set difference exists to prevent, arriving by a race instead of by arithmetic. It is narrow in this repo (ADR 0022's root-read tag exemption makes a tag-gated membership role's LIST residual unconditional too, so the divergence only materialises with the exemption off) but it is the one direction that WIDENS, and no unit test of the arithmetic can catch it - the S\\M reduction is provably correct and the bug is still there.
resolution: Check the resolved anchor role's PROVENANCE, not just the id's origin: when M is non-empty and the anchor resolves a role stamped attributes.provenance == 'supervised' (ADR 0031's stamp, already on the wire for a different purpose), drop the membership leg as STALE and fall through to the supervised-only shape - or the empty page when there is no supervised leg. Absence/unknown provenance reads as 'not supervised', so the check can only ever DROP a leg, never add one, and a role source that does not stamp behaves byte-identically to before. Generalisable rule: when a single-residual list composes scopes of different PROVENANCE, the anchor's authority must be validated, not inferred from which set its id came from - and the validation wants a marker the resolver itself stamps, not a re-derivation app-side. Coupling to record: if the provenance stamp is ever removed or renamed, this check silently becomes a no-op and the race reopens.

name: Protecting one tag key on a full-map-replace write: delta-based rejection + a separate operator entry point
description: PRODUCTION-TIER T2. To make ONE dictionary key unwritable through the public API while the resource's other tags stay freely editable, when tag writes are FULL-MAP REPLACE: (1) widen the validate method with the resource's CURRENT tags (keep the prior arity as a delegate passing {} = create semantics, so create call sites stay source-compatible); (2) compare presence-and-value over the UNION of submitted and current keys — a strip appears only on the current side and an assign only on the submitted side, so iterating either map alone misses half the moves; (3) let an ECHO pass (same value both sides, or absent both sides) — rejecting it would freeze EVERY ordinary tag edit on a resource carrying the key, and a frozen edit path is what makes people build a workaround; (4) THE FAIL-OPEN TO CLOSE: the empty-submission fast path (return empty without fetching the dictionary) may only shortcut when the CURRENT map is ALSO empty — submitting {}/null over a resource carrying the key IS a strip, and without this, strip-via-empty-map bypasses the entire check; (5) the operator's write path is a SEPARATE service entry point that never calls the delta check (validateAsOperator), never a boolean parameter a public request could reach — bypass by construction; it still validates values, and it validates only the POSTED keys, not the merged map, so an unrelated dictionary change cannot fail the one write that must work. CONSEQUENCE to state in the guide and expect in tests: a tags-CLEARING write on a TAGGED resource now consults the dictionary, so a dictionary outage makes it 503 instead of silently succeeding (fail-closed: whether the cleared key was protected is a question only the dictionary answers). This broke exactly one existing IT whose PUT submitted no tags over a tagged row and had no dictionary stub — the 503 was correct behavior, the fix was a stub bean. Cross-service back-compat detail: the flag arrives in a Jackson RECORD projection, so declare it as the Boolean WRAPPER normalized in the compact constructor — Jackson 3 THROWS on a missing primitive record component, so a primitive would 5xx every tag write against an older producer, while wrapper+normalize makes absent read as false.

name: Three-state root-attribute enrichment: enrich at ONE point (the role-lookup target), null-preserving, memoized
description:
PRODUCTION-TIER T3 / ADR 0032. To let a policy gate a CHILD decision on the GOVERNING ROOT's tags without tag inheritance, ParentRef widening, or ancestor entity loads: add one additive record component to the OPA input (AbacContext.Resource.rootAttributes, @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) @JsonProperty(root_attributes)) and populate it in the authorization manager from the governing target it ALREADY computes. Four non-obvious things. (1) NON_NULL, NEVER NON_EMPTY, and the compact constructor's defensive copy must be NULL-PRESERVING for this one component (unlike attributes/ancestors, whose null-to-empty normalization is right): the contract is THREE distinguishable states — absent = unproven (gated path closes), {} = fetched-and-untagged (opens), populated = as tagged — and both NON_EMPTY and a null-to-empty copy silently MERGE the first two in the OPEN direction. (2) Enrich at ONE point, applied to the fully-resolved check AFTER the roleResource override, keyed on 'the (type,id) the role is looked up on' — not at the two sketched insertion points (resolveInstance + the type-level branch). Both paths compute the same target, and one point makes 'root_attributes always describes the resource the role was resolved on' TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION, resolving the otherwise-ambiguous instance-check-that-also-declares-an-override case. (3) EVERY failure lands on absent — no resolution support, type-level with no override, leaf-IS-root, resolver empty, resolver THROWS (catch RuntimeException, log at debug), target reporting null attributes — and nothing propagates: a tag lookup must never become a member-facing outage, so the test asserts BOTH halves (field absent AND the decision still granted). (4) Read-through-memoize the root resolve in the existing request cache (get-before-resolve, put-after) so a request pays at most ONE extra resolver call and gate+instance see ONE coherent snapshot — but note this AMENDS the cache contract: the put is DECISION-INDEPENDENT, so an entry is a RESOLVED snapshot, no longer necessarily an AUTHORIZED one. Update the manager javadoc and the write-through comment in the same commit; what still holds is narrower and worth saying exactly: the DECIDED LEAF is always resolved fresh and never read back, so no decision can read its own cached answer. ADDITIVITY PROOF that is mechanical rather than hoped: keep compat constructors for every prior arity, and show On branch feature/void3110/production-tier
